iterations.prompt:
Create ONE two-panel pixel-art animation concept storyboard for an original military board-game opponent. This is a static pose/expression review sheet, not an implemented animation.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the established character design: preserve this exact long-faced, gaunt, comically disgruntled adult recruit, cap, T-shirt, digital camouflage, proportions, face identity, olive desk and coarse pixel-art style. Do not turn him handsome or introduce another character.
Image 2 is the user's NEW POSE DRAWING: use it for the bent arms and hand heights, not for replacing the refined face, cap or anatomy.

LAYOUT: landscape sheet, two equal panels side by side with comfortable white/off-white margins. Same character size, same camera and same tabletop height in both. Full upper body, both elbows and hands entirely visible. Small headings above the panels, exactly “대국 중” on the LEFT and “AI 패배” on the RIGHT. No game board, phone UI, extra scenes, weapons or props.

LEFT: During the board game, he changes from resting his forearms flat to the new thoughtful/tensed pose in the user's sketch. BOTH ELBOWS remain PLANTED on the tabletop, spaced apart. Forearms tilt UP inward toward his chest. The hand on the VIEWER'S LEFT is a loosely clenched fist just below his chin; the hand on the VIEWER'S RIGHT is a loosely clenched fist near the center of his chest, visibly LOWER than the other. This asymmetrical hand-height is important. Both hands are connected to anatomically clear bent forearms and elbows. No crossing arms, no palms pressing on the table, no boxing stance with floating elbows. Slight forward lean. Sour suspicious eyes, lips pursed, watching the player and thinking. Keep the cheek hollows and long angular nose. No flames yet; the established tiny amber pupils may remain.

RIGHT: The SAME AI opponent has just LOST the game to the player. Use the same planted-elbow, raised-forearm pose, with fists tightening slightly and shoulders tensing, his mouth open in a ridiculously indignant shocked shout. Two compact stylized orange/yellow/red PIXEL FLAMES burst visibly UP AND OUT from the eyes, one per eye, like a comedic arcade rage effect. Both eyes must visibly emit flames, not merely have glowing pupils. Make the flames energetic but localized around the face so his identity and cap remain readable; don't set the whole body on fire. It is a funny defeated rival, no injury, no gore, no threatening scene. A small pixel-edged speech bubble in empty space above him says EXACTLY “내가 지다니!!”, readable and not covering his face. Preserve face shape and costume between panels.

STYLE: chunky low-resolution pixel sprites, approximately 112×144 logical pixels per character, enlarged with clean square edges, bold controlled outlines, restrained flat palette, simple blocky camouflage. Hand-authored-looking clear clusters, not detailed realistic painting, no fine noisy texture, no glossy 3D. Match the input character's design while improving the hand/arm anatomy naturally. Keep the original patrol cap with flat crown and short skewed brim. Uniform has no official insignia, national flags or brand marks. Only the three Korean text strings specified above.

Radically LOWER the visual resolution of this two-pose character sheet. Redraw it as truly tiny, chunky RETRO 8-BIT GAME SPRITES, then enlarge them with nearest-neighbor. This is a major simplification, not a subtle polish.

Keep the two states, same original gaunt long-faced adult military recruit, tabletop elbow pose with one fist under chin and the other near chest, camouflage cap and T-shirt. LEFT thinking with a sour expression. RIGHT losing indignantly, both eyes emitting short cartoon flames, mouth open. Same person in both. Keep the exaggerated long chin and sunken cheeks. Keep his characterful annoyed look, not handsome, not a cute round chibi.

HARD VISUAL TARGET:
- Each complete character INCLUDING cap, entire torso, both elbows/hands and desk should look designed on ONLY a 56×72 PIXEL canvas.
- A face has only about 12–14 PIXELS ACROSS and 18 PIXELS HIGH.
- Individual logical pixels must be HUGE visible squares in the enlarged result. On a ~1500px-wide two-panel sheet, a typical logical pixel is roughly 10–12 output pixels wide.
- Maximum 10 flat colors total shared across the sheet: charcoal outline, 3 skin tones, 3 olive/khaki tones, off-white, orange and yellow. No additional blended shades.
- Eyes are 1–2 pixel slits. Nose is 2–3 pixel stepped line. Mouth is 3–4 pixels. Cheek hollow is ONE angular shadow cluster per cheek. Eliminate all little cheek wrinkles and eyelid anatomy.
- Hands are simple readable 4×5 pixel fists with only ONE division line, not individually rendered fingers.
- Military camouflage is just 4–6 BIG angular patches on the entire shirt and 2–3 on the cap. No mottling or micro-camouflage.
- Flames are bold stepped 3-color shapes, about 4×7 logical pixels each, only 1–2 detached spark squares. No gradients or realistic glow.
- Plain desk: one flat rectangle and one shadow stripe. Sleeves: simple blocks. No muscle contours, cloth wrinkles, seams, hatching, texture, dithering, small details or smoothing.
- EVERYTHING uses the SAME coarse square pixel grid. A few carefully placed flat-color blocks. Preserve readable broad shoulders, long face and clearly planted elbows.

Composition: two equal panels on plain off-white with a simple gap, no decorative borders. Small simple labels “대국 중” and “AI 패배”. One small speech bubble above the right figure: “내가 지다니!!”. Keep labels separate from sprites. Do NOT fill empty space by enlarging the logical resolution of the characters. Sparse pixels are the point.
Avoid the current image's detailed pixel painting. No high resolution artwork under a mosaic filter, no blur, antialiasing, gradients, glossy illustration or refined realistic anatomy. This should visibly resemble very small game sprites enlarged 10×, with big intentional stair steps and bold flat shapes.

Edit ONLY the RIGHT “AI 패배” panel's arm pose in this two-panel low-resolution pixel-art sheet.

Keep the LEFT “대국 중” panel completely unchanged. Preserve the RIGHT character's identity, long gaunt face, cap, camouflage T-shirt, open shouting mouth, both flaming eyes, coarse chunky low-resolution pixels, palette, desk and the exact speech “내가 지다니!!”. Keep the intentionally simplified 8-bit-like sprite style; do NOT increase detail, resolution, muscle definition, texture or shading.

RIGHT POSE CHANGE:
The defeated AI is now extremely worked up and indignantly celebrating his own outrage: BOTH ELBOWS lift completely OFF the desk and BOTH ARMS are thrown UP, fists clenched beside/above his head. Upper arms angle OUT to the sides, elbows raised to around shoulder height, forearms point UP, fists near ear/temple height. Both elbows must have a large obvious gap of empty space between them and the tabletop. NO elbows, forearms or hands touch the desk. Make the silhouette read instantly as “What?! I LOST?!” with shoulders lifted, torso slightly leaning back, mouth yelling and eyes blasting comedic pixel flames. Keep the arms clearly separate from the face and flames, and leave the speech bubble readable. Hands are simple chunky pixel fists, elbows have readable bends. Frame the entire raised-arm pose without cropping fingers or elbows. Shift the right speech bubble slightly upward if needed to leave room for the raised right-side fist, but do not alter its text.

No attack, no punching another person, no extra character or prop. Only a comically furious sore loser reacting to his board-game defeat. Keep exactly two panels. White/off-white background. Do not change the left pose, labels, costume or art style.

Edit ONLY the arm and hand pose in the LEFT “대국 중” panel of this two-panel coarse low-resolution pixel-art character sheet. Keep the entire RIGHT “AI 패배” panel unchanged, including raised arms, clenched fists, flaming eyes and “내가 지다니!!”.

LEFT POSE, anatomical sides:
1. The CHARACTER'S RIGHT arm, which appears on the VIEWER'S LEFT, keeps its elbow on the desk and forearm raised toward his chin. Replace its tightly clenched fist with a RELAXED PARTIALLY OPEN HAND. Fingers are slightly extended and loosely curved, with a little visible separation, resting casually near the chin. A thoughtful hand, not a fist, not a wave, not a pointing gesture. Use only a few coarse pixel clusters to show the relaxed fingers and thumb.
2. The CHARACTER'S LEFT arm, which appears on the VIEWER'S RIGHT, lowers from the current raised fist pose. Its ELBOW AND FOREARM rest comfortably on the TABLETOP, forearm extending inward across the table, hand relaxed near the middle. This hand is NOT clenched. The two hands must remain separate and readable.

The resulting asymmetrical pose is one relaxed raised hand near the chin, opposite forearm resting flat on the desk. Keep the same sour long face, narrow eyes, head position, patrol cap, camouflage T-shirt, entire body scale, desk, labels and framing. Make the arm connections natural while keeping the original broad silhouette.

CRITICAL STYLE LOCK: keep exactly the current CHUNKY LOW-RES pixel sprite style, same big square logical pixels and simple flat color clusters. Do NOT add detail, smaller pixels, realistic fingers, shading, texture or prettier anatomy. Simplify fingers into 2–3 stepped shapes. Do not modify the face or the other panel. No extra text, props, people or gestures.

Change ONLY the RIGHT defeated character's pose in this two-panel coarse pixel-art sheet. Keep the entire LEFT thinking character and its relaxed right hand / resting left forearm EXACTLY unchanged.

- BOTH ARMS are raised IN FRONT OF THE BODY, rather than spread outward to the left and right.

- Both elbows and all hands remain completely OFF the table, with a clear empty gap. Leave the tabletop unobstructed.

- Keep his original long gaunt face, hollow cheeks, cap, camouflage T-shirt and identity while adjusting the perspective naturally. The inner sides of the raised fists face toward his chest. Entire pose visible and no cropped hands.
